items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Morton Gould wrote me a nice little piece called called Guajiro . . . Guajira, in 7/4.

ctx.x: What was that? Can you tell us a bit more about that?

Yeah. I took a small symphony orchestra and embedded a jazz band in it. We made . . . well first of all we did . . . I got Hershey [Hershel] Kay, and we sat down and picked a repertoire of things, from [Francis] Poulenc through [Claude] Debussy, and . . . I don’t know. Let’s see . . . [Maurice] Ravel. Debussy. [Dmitri] Shostakovich, a piano sonata. [Darius] Milhaud. I don’t know. Eight composers. Morton Gould wrote me a nice little piece called called Guajiro . . . Guajira, in 7/4. Got this marvelous orchestra…
